scope: Read-only inspection of the locally installed pinned libraries and their source. This records API evidence, not an implementation or provider-configuration approval.

api_evidence.finding: AsyncOAuth2Client is an HTTPX2 AsyncClient subclass. Its forwarded client options include transport, timeout, limits, follow_redirects, max_redirects, proxy, trust_env, verify and related request settings.

Direct create_authorization_url(url, state, code_verifier, ...) returns (authorization_url, state). With code_challenge_method='S256' and a supplied verifier it adds the S256 challenge. Supplying application-generated state, verifier and nonce avoids the Starlette helper's code-verifier debug log.

Direct fetch_token(fixed_token_endpoint, grant_type='authorization_code', code=..., code_verifier=..., redirect_uri=...) prepares and posts the form. Omit state when the application validates the callback state itself; state is used by Authlib when parsing a complete authorization_response. Inspected implementation has no log call that prints authorization code, token response, verifier or token request body.

The Starlette OAuth wrapper fetches discovery and merges metadata into client kwargs. Its authorization helper logs the generated code_verifier at DEBUG. Avoid this helper for a strict no-secret-logs contract, and do not allow discovery metadata to override trusted HTTP client policy.

Built-in discovery/JWKS helpers call request() then resp.json(), buffering the response without a configured byte limit. parse_id_token uses joserfc jwt.decode, KeySet.import_key_set and JWSRegistry; its algorithm list comes from discovery (default RS256), strict_check_header=False, and default claim options constrain issuer only. Supply fixed application algorithm policy and explicit issuer/audience claim options if using this validation path.

The code-flow ID token requires iss, sub, aud, exp and iat; validates nbf when present, nonce when provided, and azp consistency. Default audience validation is not pinned to the configured client_id unless an explicit aud claims_option is supplied. azp is required by the helper when the audience is not the single client_id; it is not unconditionally required for a matching single audience.

api_evidence.source: httpx2/_client.py:1450-1505; httpx2/_models.py:AsyncByteStream and Response stream APIs
api_evidence.finding: HTTPX2 defaults follow_redirects=False but trust_env=True and max_redirects=20. Set all relevant values explicitly (including trust_env=False, proxy=None, finite timeout/limits, follow_redirects=False and max_redirects=0). A size limit must count streamed bytes; Content-Length alone does not protect chunked responses. The inspected Authlib calls do not expose streaming before JSON parsing, so a capped stream/transport or bounded custom HTTP client is required.

api_evidence.source: httpx2/_client.py:1480-1505; httpx2/_transports/default.py AsyncHTTPTransport; HTTPX2 MockTransport API
api_evidence.finding: HTTPX2 accepts an AsyncBaseTransport, including MockTransport for request-level tests. Authlib's wrapper creates and closes separate clients for discovery, token and JWKS operations; reusing a normal AsyncHTTPTransport object as client_kwargs across those clients risks it being closed after the first client. A managed transport factory/client override or equivalent lifecycle design is needed. A MockTransport has a no-op close and is reusable for tests.

HTTPX2 logs method, URL and response status at INFO; HTTPCore2 DEBUG trace logs operation names, trace fields and exceptions. The inspected direct Authlib authorization/token methods do not log code, token, verifier or request body. Keep endpoint URLs free of credential-bearing query strings, avoid attaching traces that emit sensitive data, and retain application-level redaction.

official_references.use: Authlib Starlette client integration and documented callback helpers; local source inspection is the authority for pinned 1.9.1 implementation details.

unresolved_contract_questions: Exact maximum response bytes for discovery, JWKS and token responses, and whether the cap applies to decoded/decompressed bytes, need explicit contract values. Authlib's standard request().json() path does not enforce a cap.

Exact configured-origin matching and a transport lifecycle compatible with separate Authlib clients need implementation-level specification; HTTPS alone does not bind an endpoint to an approved origin.
Clarify whether azp must always be present or only when required by OIDC audience rules; Authlib's default validation uses the latter behavior.
limitations: No service, provider, or network was contacted; no runtime request was executed.
